investigations.name: basement-membrane-v1
investigations.title: Basement membrane v1 — collagen IV network modulus & remodelling for the AICS vertex model
investigations.description:
This investigation is the clean-room Vivarium build of the AICS-Lumenoids
"Basement membrane — v1 model specification" (Roam graph, exported 2026-09-30;
the source spec and diagram are in `workspace/references/`). Every model
parameter is transcribed from the spec's parameter sheet and labelled as such.
The authors' LAMMPS input scripts are now public
(github.com/Billie1717/BasementMembraneTurnoverSims, Zenodo
10.5281/zenodo.20719515, commit `ab4c004`); this build remains a transcription
from the spec rather than a port of those scripts, and they are the ground
truth to cross-check its parameters against (not yet done — decision below).

**Engines.** The workspace imports two already-wrapped simulators —
`viva-lammps` (the `LAMMPSProcess` bridge) and `viva-smoldyn` — and builds the
collagen IV network on top of the real LAMMPS engine. LAMMPS runs stages 1–2
(rigid rods, junction flexibility); Smoldyn is held for stage 3 (flexible
fibers + surface binders) per spec decision #2.

**Staged build (spec "v1 build").**
  - Stage 1 — reproduce the paper; separate elastic from viscous. Stretch,
    hold, then switch the crosslink chemistry on. Reports an elastic modulus
    and a stress-relaxation time.  ← this investigation's first study.
  - Stage 2 — growing substrate (flat): impose equibiaxial strain rate ε̇,
    read off σ(ε̇); an effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ and the rate at which the
    response turns elastic.
  - Stage 3 — add the cell–BM linker (surface-attached springs, constant
    off-rate). Smoldyn's surface binders land here.
  - Stage 4 — curvature (only if stages 2–3 depend on R beyond ε̇ = Ṙ/R).

**Coupling route (spec decision).** Offline first: tabulate the BM's modulus
and remodelling time against growth rate and hand them to the vertex model.
Then direct: vertex-mesh surface velocities drive the BM substrate, BM stress
feeds back, exchanged every N vertex steps.
